ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 2 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Mahatma Gandhi

code.originalText: Four-week blood pressure review and planning for a fast he intends to keep, with clinical nutrition consultation

text.paragraph: Four-week blood pressure review; planning for a fast next month; clinical nutrition consultation today. [S]

Mr. Gandhi returns four weeks after starting amlodipine 2.5 mg. He takes it each morning and has had no ankle swelling, flushing, or dizziness. He measures his own blood pressure twice a day; his home average is 148/86. He keeps his usual diet of goat's milk, curd, fruit, nuts, vegetables, and whole grains with little salt, and walks 5 km each morning. He tells us he intends to begin a seven-day fast of conscience in two weeks, taking only water with a little salt and citrus juice. He has thought about it carefully, understands the risks we described at the first visit, and asks for help to keep it as safely as possible. He had an echocardiogram and a bone density scan this morning and saw the dietitian. [S]

list.item:
Stage 2 hypertension (I10). Office 146/84 and home average 148/86 mmHg, improved from 168/94 but above the goal of below 130/80. Echocardiogram today shows mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy with an ejection fraction of 62%, which strengthens the case for reaching goal. [S]
Increase amlodipine to 5 mg daily.
Hold amlodipine on fast days and whenever standing systolic pressure is below 110 or he is dizzy on standing.
Home readings lying and standing twice a day during the fast.

Vitamin B12 deficiency (E53.8). Serum B12 238 pg/mL is low-normal, but methylmalonic acid is raised at 0.48 umol/L, with hemoglobin 12.8 g/dL and MCV 99 fL. His diet supplies little B12; goat's milk contains less than cow's milk. [S]
Start vitamin B12 1 mg by mouth daily.
Recheck B12, methylmalonic acid, and blood count in three to four months.

Vitamin D deficiency (E55.9). 25-hydroxyvitamin D 19 ng/mL. [S]
Start vitamin D3 1000 units daily.
Recheck in three to four months.

Low bone mass (M85.80). DXA today: lumbar spine T-score -1.4 and femoral neck -2.2. FRAX 10-year risk 8.6% for a major osteoporotic fracture and 2.6% for hip fracture, below the treatment thresholds of 20% and 3%. [S]
No osteoporosis drug now.
Calcium from food, vitamin D, walking, and balance exercise.
Repeat DXA in two years.

Underweight; planned fast (R63.6). BMI 17.0. He has full capacity and has made an informed decision to fast, which we respect. A seven-day fast at his weight will put him at high risk of refeeding problems, so the plan is built to reduce harm rather than to dissuade him. [S]
Fast safety plan and refeeding protocol agreed with him and the dietitian (see care plan).
Clinic visit the morning after the fast, before the first meal.
Hospital admission for refeeding offered; he would rather refeed at home with close follow-up.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: 2025 AHA/ACC/AANP/AAPA/ABC/ACCP/ACPM/AGS/AMA/ASPC/NMA/PCNA/SGIM Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults (2025); Indian guidelines on hypertension-IV (2019) (2019); Nutrition support for adults: oral nutrition support, enteral tube feeding and parenteral nutrition (CG32) (2006, updated 2017); ASPEN Consensus Recommendations for Refeeding Syndrome (2020); The clinician's guide to prevention and treatment of osteoporosis (2022); Falls Prevention in Community-Dwelling Older Adults: Interventions (2024); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, hypertension and osteoporosis monographs (2026)

Follow-up: Daily telephone check during the fast. Clinic visit the morning after the fast ends, before the first meal, with electrolytes. Next scheduled visit 2026-04-13: review the morning after a seven-day fast, before the first meal: refeeding risk assessment and start of refeeding. [S]
